title: CARE arXiv paper
summary: Public arXiv source for CARE, describing auditable control of LLM-generated policies in scientific experimentation.
content: arXiv:2606.14581. Title: CARE: Controlling LLM-Generated Policies through Auditable Review of Evidence in Scientific Experimentation.

title: CARE
summary: CARE keeps a non-LLM incumbent optimizer as the default action path and allows LLM-generated challenger policies only through a public-evidence intervention gate.
content: The paper evaluates CARE on Minerva/Olympus and ChemLex benchmarks. The key system idea is to separate creative proposal generation from auditable intervention approval.

title: High-throughput experiment optimization
summary: Sequentially choose experimental conditions from a finite candidate pool under a limited reveal budget.
content: The task setting covers reaction condition optimization with candidates such as ligand, catalyst, solvent, temperature, and substrate combinations. Objectives may include yield, selectivity, conversion, or cost-adjusted score.

title: Minerva/Olympus Suzuki coupling benchmark
summary: A Suzuki coupling finite-pool benchmark used in the CARE paper.
content: The CARE paper reports a 5,670-candidate replay setting with 30 matched seeds, 5 initial observations, and 10 reveal rounds. This public card records the benchmark interface; raw candidate tables are not included in this repository.

title: ChemLex acid-amine benchmark
summary: A reaction optimization benchmark used in the CARE paper.
content: The CARE paper reports a ChemLex replay setting for acid-amine combinations. This card tracks the dataset role in CARE experiments; raw candidate tables are not included in this repository.

title: Synthetic ChemLex-style acid-amine replay
summary: A synthetic acid-amine finite-pool task used to test whether the same CARE replay loop works beyond Suzuki-style candidates.
content: The adapter creates acid, amine, solvent polarity, base equivalent, and temperature combinations with hidden yield values. It is a smoke-test dataset only; it should be replaced with release-safe real ChemLex candidate tables for paper-level reproduction.

title: Dreher-Doyle Buchwald-Hartwig HTE dataset
summary: A public high-throughput Buchwald-Hartwig reaction yield dataset used as a real finite-pool replay task.
content: The adapter reads Ligand, Additive, Base, Aryl halide, and Output from the public rxn4chemistry/rxn_yields workbook. The raw Excel file is downloaded locally at runtime and is not committed to this repository.

title: Perera Suzuki-Miyaura HTE dataset
summary: A public high-throughput Suzuki-Miyaura reaction yield dataset used as a real finite-pool replay task.
content: The adapter reads reactants, catalyst, ligand, reagent, solvent, and Product_Yield_PCT_Area_UV from the public rxn4chemistry/rxn_yields workbook. The raw Excel file is downloaded locally at runtime and is not committed to this repository.

title: Synthetic materials formulation replay
summary: A synthetic materials optimization task for testing CARE-style gated decisions outside reaction yield optimization.
content: The adapter creates dopant, composition ratio, annealing temperature, and dwell time combinations with a hidden stability score. It is intended to exercise the same audit and gate code on a materials-like objective before real release-safe materials data is connected.

title: Public-evidence intervention gate
summary: The gate compares incumbent and challenger proposals before outcome reveal and authorizes intervention only when pre-selection evidence supports the change.
content: A gate certificate should record the incumbent candidate, challenger candidate, evidence used, checks passed or failed, and the final accept/reject decision. The gate should not use hidden outcomes from the current reveal.

title: Audit log
summary: A replay trace that records each decision, gate certificate, reveal, and knowledge update.
content: The synthetic replay harness emits audit entries so each selected candidate can be inspected after the run. This is useful for debugging unsafe interventions and measuring rejected-good-challenger cases.

title: SkillCard
summary: A structured representation for reusable scientific decision heuristics.
content: In the replay smoke test, SkillCard objects define bounded policy adjustments such as ligand prior, ligand risk penalty, and diversity exploration. The goal is to keep skill effects inspectable and auditable.

title: Embedding retrieval over CARE cards
summary: A vector search layer over structured CARE knowledge cards.
content: The prototype embeds each card using title, summary, content, tags, source ids, and related ids. The local hashed provider is for development; production use should call an OpenAI-compatible /v1/embeddings endpoint and store model metadata with each vector.

title: Ligand prior skill
summary: A simple ranking prior that favors ligand identities associated with higher synthetic yields in the public/observed context.
content: The synthetic replay harness includes a ligand prior as a minimal example of a bounded, auditable policy skill. Real datasets should replace synthetic coefficients with evidence-derived rules.

title: Replace synthetic replay adapter
summary: Swap the synthetic Suzuki-like candidate pool with real Minerva/Olympus and ChemLex candidate tables when release-safe data is available.
content: The current experiment validates the CARE 2.0 software loop. The next step is to implement dataset adapters for real finite-pool replay and reproduce CARE paper baselines under matched seeds.

title: Connect a real embedding endpoint
summary: Use an OpenAI-compatible embedding model to build semantic retrieval over CARE cards.
content: Set CARE_OPENAI_API_KEY, CARE_OPENAI_BASE_URL, and CARE_EMBEDDING_MODEL, then run build_embeddings.py with --provider openai. A chat-only model endpoint is not enough; the service must expose /v1/embeddings.

title: Awesome AI for Chemistry
summary: A curated chemistry AI paper/resource list with a Generalized Model/Datasets section.
content: Useful leads include Open Reaction Database, QM-series datasets, reaction design resources, and robotic chemist/automation references. Best used for expanding CARE's knowledge base and selecting additional public benchmark candidates.

title: Awesome LLM-Centric Molecular Discovery
summary: A curated list of LLM-centric molecular discovery methods and datasets.
content: The dataset table includes PubChem, ChEMBL, ZINC, Dockstring, MoleculeNet, QM9, MOSES, and related resources. Dockstring, MoleculeNet, and QM9 are practical next candidates for CARE finite-pool replay.

title: Awesome Materials-Aware Large Language Models
summary: A curated list of materials-aware LLM work across data extraction, property prediction, synthesis planning, and agent-driven laboratory systems.
content: This is not primarily a runnable dataset list. It is useful for populating CARE's knowledge base with materials-aware extraction methods, property prediction models, synthesis planning papers, and lab-agent design patterns.

title: Awesome LLM4EDA
summary: A curated EDA-focused LLM list with useful analogies for verification and gated generation.
content: This is not a chemistry or materials dataset source. It is useful for CARE architecture analogies: generated proposal, deterministic checks, simulator or verifier, audit trail, and rejection when evidence fails.

title: Dockstring
summary: A virtual-screening dataset candidate for finite-pool molecular discovery replay.
content: Dockstring can be framed as selecting molecules from a finite pool to maximize a docking-derived objective. It is a practical next dataset because it aligns with molecular discovery and does not require wet-lab yield tables.

title: MoleculeNet
summary: A molecular property benchmark collection; the ESOL/Delaney subset is now connected as finite-pool property replay.
content: MoleculeNet is useful for CARE if we select a single property task, treat measured property values as hidden outcomes, and evaluate sequential candidate selection. The current adapter uses ESOL/Delaney measured log solubility, normalized to a 0-100 score. It is less directly experimental than HTE yield data but useful for molecular discovery search.

title: MoleculeNet ESOL Delaney solubility
summary: A connected public molecular property replay dataset using measured log solubility.
content: The adapter downloads delaney-processed.csv from DeepChem's public MoleculeNet data hosting. Each candidate is a molecule with SMILES and molecular descriptors. The hidden target is normalized measured log solubility, using a fixed logS range rather than dataset min/max.

title: QM9
summary: A quantum chemistry molecular property dataset suitable for finite-pool property search.
content: QM9 is useful for cross-domain molecular property optimization. It is not an HTE reaction dataset, but CARE can still test sequential property search over a finite pool.

title: Open Reaction Database
summary: A public reaction data source for reaction knowledge extraction and possible measured-yield replay subsets.
content: ORD is best used first as a knowledge source. For replay, we should select a clean measured-yield subset with consistent fields and explicit outcomes, then build a dataset adapter.

title: Public factor evidence model
summary: A stronger public-observation model for real finite-pool replay.
content: The replay baseline now scores candidates using smoothed means over all revealed decision factors, not only the main group column. The gate can apply bounded factor-level adjustments only when revealed outcomes repeatedly support a factor.

title: Add molecular property replay adapters
summary: Add one molecular discovery dataset beyond reaction HTE.
content: The next practical adapter should use Dockstring, MoleculeNet, or QM9. Dockstring is the closest to discovery-style optimization; MoleculeNet and QM9 are useful for property search but less experimental.

title: Kimi-Lex dataset request
summary: Dataset requested for the next CARE 2.0 experiment pass; implementation is blocked until the download link and schema are available.
content: Needed before implementation: download URL, license or redistribution boundary, file format, candidate columns, public observable fields, hidden target, objective, and replay budget. Group sync owner split: Weiyi provides the link; Franklin builds the adapter and runs replay.

title: Materials Project replay request
summary: Materials Project pathway for CARE 2.0 cross-domain materials replay.
content: Needed before implementation: access mode, target property, candidate representation, public features, raw-cache policy, and replay framing. Candidate targets include band gap, formation energy, stability, or synthesis success. Raw API responses should not be committed until the release boundary is explicit.

title: Document-guided six-adapter replay sweep
summary: Tracked replay sweep over synthetic Suzuki, synthetic ChemLex, synthetic materials, real Buchwald-Hartwig, real Suzuki-Miyaura, and MoleculeNet ESOL.
content: Run command: python3 experiments/care_replay/scripts/run_synthetic_suzuki.py --dataset all --seeds 30 --rounds 10 --initial 5. Synthetic adapters show clear positive movement from gated skill/evidence loops; real HTE adapters are mostly neutral under the conservative public-evidence gate; ESOL gives a small positive signal for molecular property replay.

title: Full replay outputs and raw data
summary: Tracked full output directory for the 2026-06-28 CARE 2.0 replay sweep.
content: Artifacts live under experiments/care_replay/outputs, experiments/care_replay/data/raw, and experiments/care_replay/results/2026-06-28-doc-guided-sweep. The tracked outputs include raw public data, summaries, metrics tables, 540 per-mode/per-seed audit logs, and 540 per-mode/per-seed knowledge snapshots.

title: Factor evidence can transfer across related finite-pool tasks
summary: A task-level hypothesis that factor-level public evidence learned in one reaction replay can help a related reaction replay after confidence discounting.
content: The transferable unit should not be a raw chemical rule such as 'this ligand is always good'. It should be an auditable decision pattern: observed factor support, effect direction, support count, confidence, counterexamples, and bounded adjustment. The hypothesis should first be tested on BH-to-Suzuki before broader chemical-to-material transfer claims.

title: BH-to-Suzuki confidence-discount transfer
summary: Near-domain transfer plan from Buchwald-Hartwig factor evidence to Suzuki-Miyaura replay.
content: Proposed transfer path: learn public factor evidence from Buchwald-Hartwig, abstract it into a support/confidence card, discount by reaction-domain distance, apply only bounded adjustments in Suzuki, and let the evidence gate authorize or reject each challenger. Compare no-transfer baseline versus transferred-skill-plus-gate on matched seeds.

title: Ablation experiment review
summary: Review item for choosing the first CARE 2.0 ablation experiments.
content: Candidate ablations: no-transfer versus BH-to-Suzuki transfer; gate_v1 versus gate_v2; factor-evidence ranker only versus risk penalty only versus diversity only; with/without public factor evidence on real HTE datasets; synthetic priors versus evidence-derived adjustments.

title: Knowledge-base schema review
summary: Review item for checking whether the extended card types are sufficient for CARE 2.0 transfer experiments.
content: The current schema now includes hypothesis, transfer, experiment_result, run_log, dataset_request, and review card types. Review should check whether these are enough for future automatic skill compilation from audit logs and whether additional fields are needed beyond the common card schema.

title: Matbench experimental band gap
summary: A public real materials composition-property dataset used as a finite-pool experimental band-gap replay task.
content: The adapter downloads matbench_expt_gap.json.gz, parses composition strings into public material descriptors, and treats normalized experimental band gap as the hidden objective revealed only after selection. The first implementation uses composition-only public features and no fixed preferred material-family prior.

title: Materials baseline and no-gate ablation
summary: A two-dataset materials replay pass with no-CARE random baseline, public greedy incumbent, no-gate challenger, and gated CARE variants.
content: Run commands: python3 experiments/care_replay/scripts/run_synthetic_suzuki.py --dataset synthetic_materials_i --seeds 30 --rounds 10 --initial 5; python3 experiments/care_replay/scripts/run_synthetic_suzuki.py --dataset real_matbench_expt_gap --seeds 30 --rounds 10 --initial 5. Synthetic materials follows the expected ordering: random < incumbent < skill/challenger. Real Matbench experimental band gap is diagnostic: no_care_random slightly beats the current composition-only public greedy and CARE variants, indicating the need for stronger materials descriptors or a surrogate observation model.

title: Commonstack LLM-in-the-loop replay
summary: First CARE replay pass with real Commonstack LLM calls producing auditable factor-level policy adjustments.
content: Run on synthetic_materials_i and real_matbench_expt_gap with 3 seeds, 6 reveal rounds, and modes no_care_random, incumbent, llm_no_gate, and llm_gate_v1. The LLM model was openai/gpt-4o-mini via an OpenAI-compatible Commonstack endpoint. Audit logs store raw model responses, parsed JSON policies, applied factor adjustments, model names, and usage metadata. Synthetic materials shows a small improvement over the incumbent; real Matbench shows no final-best gain yet, but the gate removes bad interventions from LLM proposals.

title: MoleculeNet FreeSolv hydration free energy
summary: A connected public molecular-property replay dataset using experimental hydration free energy.
content: The adapter downloads SAMPL.csv from DeepChem's public MoleculeNet data hosting. Each candidate is a molecule with SMILES-derived public descriptor bins. The hidden target is a fixed-scale hydration-affinity score where more negative experimental hydration free energy is better.

title: MoleculeNet Lipophilicity
summary: A connected public molecular-property replay dataset using experimental lipophilicity.
content: The adapter downloads Lipophilicity.csv from DeepChem's public MoleculeNet data hosting. Each candidate is a molecule with SMILES-derived public descriptor bins. The hidden target is a fixed-scale normalized experimental lipophilicity score.

title: Nine-dataset CARE 2.0 generalization sweep
summary: A broad replay sweep over synthetic controls, real HTE, real molecular-property, and real materials-property datasets with no-CARE, incumbent, no-gate, and gated CARE2 modes.
content: Run command: python3 experiments/care_replay/scripts/run_synthetic_suzuki.py --dataset all --seeds 30 --rounds 10 --initial 5 --modes no_care_random,incumbent,no_gate,gate_v1,gate_v2. The sweep added FreeSolv and Lipophilicity to the existing synthetic Suzuki, synthetic ChemLex, synthetic materials, Buchwald-Hartwig, Suzuki-Miyaura, ESOL, and Matbench adapters. Synthetic controls show clear positive gains. Real HTE is mostly neutral. ESOL is modestly positive. FreeSolv has a small no-gate gain that the gate mostly removes. Lipophilicity is slightly negative. Matbench remains diagnostic because random search beats the current composition-only public incumbent.

title: Nine-dataset CommonStack LLM generalization sweep
summary: A CARE 2.0 replay sweep over nine datasets using real CommonStack LLM calls for llm_no_gate and llm_gate_v1 modes.
content: Run command: python3 experiments/care_replay/scripts/run_synthetic_suzuki.py --dataset all --seeds 5 --rounds 6 --initial 5 --modes no_care_random,incumbent,llm_no_gate,llm_gate_v1 --llm-model openai/gpt-4o-mini --output-tag llm_commonstack_5seed. The run produced 270 real LLM call records across synthetic controls, real HTE datasets, MoleculeNet ESOL/FreeSolv/Lipophilicity, and Matbench experimental band gap. All parsed successfully with non-empty applied specs. Results are mixed: Buchwald-Hartwig, Lipophilicity with gate, Matbench vs incumbent, ChemLex no-gate, and synthetic materials with gate show positive signals; Suzuki-Miyaura shows a harmful no-gate LLM proposal that the gate blocks; FreeSolv and synthetic Suzuki are negative or slightly negative. The main takeaway is that actual LLM proposals need gate control and stronger observation models for reliable cross-domain transfer.

title: ChemLex Acid-Amine wetlab conversion
summary: A connected public wetlab acid-amine conversion dataset from the updated ChemLex Zenodo record.
content: The adapter downloads Chemlex_Acidamine_Wetlab_Data.xlsx from Zenodo record 17596563. It exposes anonymized acid, amine, reagent, and solvent labels as public decision factors and treats conversion_value as the hidden target revealed only after selection. The table has 11,669 rows in the updated v3 record.

title: Real ChemLex Acid-Amine wetlab replay
summary: A real ChemLex replay pass showing that the current public observation model underperforms random search.
content: Non-LLM run: 30 seeds, 10 reveal rounds, modes no_care_random, incumbent, no_gate, gate_v1, and gate_v2. LLM run: 5 seeds, 6 reveal rounds, modes no_care_random, incumbent, llm_no_gate, and llm_gate_v1 with 30 real CommonStack LLM calls and zero parse errors. The key result is negative: no_care_random reaches final-best mean 90.381 in the 30-seed run, while incumbent and gated CARE variants are near 82.13. In the 5-seed LLM run, random remains strongest and LLM modes do not improve over incumbent.

title: BH-to-Suzuki transfer-card ablation
summary: The first explicit CARE 2.0 cross-domain transfer experiment from Buchwald-Hartwig to Suzuki-Miyaura.
content: Run command: python3 experiments/care_replay/scripts/run_transfer_ablation.py --source-dataset real_buchwald_hartwig --target-dataset real_suzuki_miyaura --seeds 30 --rounds 10 --initial 5 --source-observations 48 --discount 0.65 --output-tag bh_to_suzuki_30seed. The transfer card maps BH ligand/base/aryl_halide/additive roles to Suzuki ligand/reagent/reactant_1/solvent roles. This is real source-to-target transfer, but the first implementation is negative: target incumbent final-best mean is 92.6085, while transfer_no_gate and transfer_gate_v1 are 91.3879 and transfer_plus_local_gate_v1 is 91.6643. The next iteration needs richer descriptors and a transfer-specific risk gate.
